endorsements.quote: The opportunities and challenges provide a foundation for collaborative teams of GPs, IT professionals, and data scientists, whose involvement is essential at every stage of developing, validating, and implementing an AI/ML-based diagnostic prediction model [ 3 , 7 , 33 ].
New tools should be developed in close collaboration with GPs, focus on real-world clinical problems, and be rigorously validated in general practice settings.
Prediction tools should ideally integrate into electronic health records, providing real-time risk scores or alerts to be truly useful for GPs [ 3 ].

unlisted_practices: Use independent datasets for external validation of diagnostic prediction models before implementation in daily practice.
Examine datasets carefully for potential biases during early development of diagnostic prediction tools.
Report developed diagnostic prediction tools using frameworks such as TRIPOD-AI.
Handle outputs of diagnostic prediction tools that lack EU MDR certification cautiously.
Ensure diagnostic prediction tools focus on clinically relevant problems for general practice.
GPs should take a leading role in the development, validation, and implementation of diagnostic prediction models.

screen.reason: This is a commentary/perspective article examining the utility and challenges of AI/ML diagnostic prediction models in general practice and offering recommendations for development and implementation.
